description: 'FliY is a bifunctional flagellar motor switch protein that acts as a
  CheY-P phosphatase localized at the flagellar C-ring. It contains three functional
  domains: an N-terminal CheY-binding region homologous to FliM residues 6-15, a middle
  CheC-like phosphatase domain with conserved Glu/Asn catalytic residues, and a C-terminal
  FliN-like domain that integrates it into the flagellar switch complex. FliY catalyzes
  the dephosphorylation of the phosphorylated response regulator CheY-P at the site
  of its action (the flagellar motor), thereby contributing to signal termination
  in the chemotaxis pathway. B. subtilis uses a three-phosphatase system (CheC, FliY,
  CheX) instead of the CheZ found in E. coli. FliY functions constitutively to maintain
  optimal CheY-P levels near the motor, while CheC responds to attractant stimuli.
  FliY can complement Salmonella fliN mutants, confirming its structural role in the
  C-ring.'

        CheY-P hydrolysis in vitro. The domain architecture (CheC-like 
        phosphatase domain) and structural studies further support this 
        function.

        modulates the duration of enhanced CheY-P levels and thereby regulates 
        switching between clockwise and counterclockwise flagellar rotation.

    original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000002
    review:
      summary: IEA annotation based on InterPro domain IPR001172 
        (FliN_T3SS_HrcQb). This annotation is problematic because FliY is not 
        itself a motor protein - it is a component of the motor switch that 
        regulates motor activity, but does not generate force or movement 
        directly.
      action: REMOVE
      reason: This is an over-annotation. FliY is a component of the flagellar 
        motor switch complex (C-ring) but it does not have motor activity 
        itself. The motor activity is generated by the stator units (MotA/MotB) 
        interacting with FliG. FliY's role is to modulate CheY-P levels, not to 
        generate rotational force. The InterPro domain hit is based on FliN 
        homology, but FliN is a switch component, not a motor per se. The term 
        "cytoskeletal motor activity" implies direct force generation, which 
        FliY does not perform.

document.description: FliY is a bifunctional flagellar motor switch protein that acts as a CheY-P phosphatase localized at the flagellar C-ring. It contains three functional domains: an N-terminal CheY-binding region homologous to FliM residues 6-15, a middle CheC-like phosphatase domain with conserved Glu/Asn catalytic residues, and a C-terminal FliN-like domain that integrates it into the flagellar switch complex. FliY catalyzes the dephosphorylation of the phosphorylated response regulator CheY-P at the site of its action (the flagellar motor), thereby contributing to signal termination in the chemotaxis pathway. B. subtilis uses a three-phosphatase system (CheC, FliY, CheX) instead of the CheZ found in E. coli. FliY functions constitutively to maintain optimal CheY-P levels near the motor, while CheC responds to attractant stimuli. FliY can complement Salmonella fliN mutants, confirming its structural role in the C-ring.
